clue.text: Like green area — reverse of awful desert

indicators.note: something awful is in a bad state, so the letters that follow are in disorder

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A green, leafy place is described as the opposite of a terrible desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reverse' tempts a solver to write a word backwards, but nothing is reversed: it only joins the surface, since FORESTED land is the opposite of desert. The fodder includes 'of'.
explanation.definitionFit: A forested region is covered in trees, so it is a green area on any map.

clue.text: Otherwise name is inserted in personal record, as usual

parts.note: 'or' means otherwise, as in 'or else'

indicators.note: inserted means put inside, so the name goes within the personal record

parts.note: a diary is a personal daily record
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Someone's name gets entered in their personal file, as is routine.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ordinary is normal and commonplace, which is what usual means.

clue.text: Complication with people following magical symbol not starting on time

indicators.note: a thing not starting has lost its opening, so the word's first letter goes
the people are placed coming after the magical symbol in the answer

parts.note: a pentangle is a five-pointed star used in magic
men are people
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A wizard's ritual goes wrong when the crowd arrives after the pentagram, not starting punctually.
explanation.definitionFit: An entanglement is a tangled situation, a difficulty or complication.

clue.text: Cheap tea — said where it may be found

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word before it counts for its sound alone

parts.note: the letter T is pronounced like tea
tea is found in a pot

explanation.surface: Cheap tea, and a remark about where you would find it.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'it' in the second half points back at the letter: T sits IN POT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinpot is a dismissive adjective for something cheap, inferior or petty.

clue.text: Old fogey's repeated urge to perform

indicators.note: repeated asks for the same piece twice, one copy after another

parts.note: 'Do!' is an imperative urging someone to act
the same piece a second time

explanation.surface: An elderly stick-in-the-mud keeps feeling the urge to go on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodo, the extinct bird, is slang for an old-fashioned person out of touch with the times.

clue.text: Critically discussed member of clergy that is married

parts.note: Rev is short for reverend
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is
wed means married

explanation.surface: A married vicar became the subject of critical gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: A book or play that is reviewed has been assessed in print by a critic.

clue.text: This kept same text, ultimately?

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so each word yields its final letter

parts.note: the closing letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: A proofreader's question about which mark leaves a passage unchanged.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stet, Latin for 'let it stand', is the editor's mark cancelling a correction so the original wording remains.

clue.text: Start off carelessly, and with little effort to be honest

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which alone is kept

parts.note: the opening letter
taken as written
doing something idly means putting little effort in

explanation.surface: Admitting frankly that one began a job sloppily and lazily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Start off' reads like a phrasal verb, but it only picks the first letter of the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Candidly means frankly or openly, the adverb used when owning up honestly.

clue.text: Musical work to repeat with variation

indicators.note: variation means altering the order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: both words, letter for letter

explanation.surface: A composer's theme that comes back with variations, as in a set of musical variations.
explanation.definitionFit: An operetta is a light opera, a piece of musical theatre.

clue.text: Ready to publish what's in daily, twice? Just the opposite

indicators.note: the opposite way round means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: the tide comes in twice a day

explanation.surface: Seems to ask what appears twice in a daily newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Daily' suggests a newspaper, but here it is the plain adverb: the sea comes in twice daily.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit copy is to correct and prepare it for publication, getting it ready to print.

clue.text: Reckoned without precision as a quietly expert team won game

parts.note: taken as written
p, piano, is the musical mark for quietly
a pro is an expert
a cricket or football side has eleven players, XI in Roman numerals
in chess, a player who has mated the opponent has won

explanation.surface: Someone estimated roughly that a quiet, skilled side had won.
explanation.definitionFit: To approximate is to estimate a figure roughly rather than calculate it exactly.

clue.text: Kiwi, for example, unfortunately trapped by European

indicators.note: something trapped is held inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: an Austrian is a European
alas expresses regret, much as unfortunately does

explanation.surface: A kiwi bird, sadly, has been caught by someone from Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: Kiwi is the informal name for a New Zealander, and New Zealand is part of Australasia.
explanation.definitionFit: A New Zealander is a native of Australasia, so 'Kiwi' is one example of the adjective.

clue.text: Violent criminal ousting many from Germany full of dread

indicators.note: a thing full of another holds it inside
ousting throws something out, so those letters are removed from the country's name

parts.note: the country, written in full
taken as written, then removed
angst is a feeling of dread

explanation.surface: A thug expelled crowds from Germany in a climate of fear.
explanation.definitionFit: A gangster is a member of a criminal gang, typically using violence.

clue.text: Some golf balls are like this

definitions.text: Some golf balls are like this

parts.words: Some golf balls are like this
parts.note: surface reading: a remark on the shape or type of certain golf balls
setter's reading: all golf balls are spherical, and some are also played in a single golfing session

explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' is the joke: every golf ball is spherical, so the qualifier points to the other sense, the balls used in one game on the course.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means spherical, and also a complete game of eighteen holes in golf.

clue.text: Desired weight I lost

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for weight
taken as written
to shed something is to lose it

explanation.surface: A dieter's wish: the weight I've lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Wished and desired are synonyms, both past tenses of wanting something.

clue.text: Exhaust, we hear, or other part of car

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the word is matched by pronunciation not spelling

parts.note: to tire someone is to exhaust them

explanation.surface: Listing car components: the exhaust, or some other bit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exhaust' looks like the car part, which is why the definition says 'other'; it is really the verb meaning wear out. Tyre is the British spelling of tire.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyre is the rubber covering on a car's wheel, a different component from the exhaust.

clue.text: Reduce volume of refuse

definitions.meaning: first meaning: lower the sound, as with a dial

explanation.surface: Turning the sound down on a pile of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like the noun meaning rubbish, but it is the verb meaning reject.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to lower a setting such as volume and to decline a request.

clue.text: Repeatedly strike for hard cash these days

definitions.meaning: first meaning: hit hard again and again
second meaning: the British unit of currency, now a coin

explanation.surface: Someone hammering away to get paid in cash.
explanation.walkthrough: The pound note was withdrawn in England, so these days the pound is a metal coin, hence 'hard'.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means beat heavily, and the noun is the UK currency unit, nowadays issued as a coin.

clue.text: Weed, before spring, having no room to grow

parts.note: weed and pot are both slang for cannabis
to bound is to leap or spring

explanation.surface: A gardener's note about weeds sprouting before spring in cramped beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Weed' and 'spring' both sit in a garden picture, but one is a drug and the other a leap.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot-bound plant has roots filling its container, leaving it no space to grow further.

clue.text: Bank that's really heartless

indicators.note: without a heart, the middle of the word is removed

parts.note: taken as written before losing its centre

explanation.surface: A bank that's truly without compassion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' is the verb, as in bank on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: To bank on something is to count on or depend on it, the same as relying.

clue.text: Lethargic and liable to forget some shopping?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, punning: someone without a shopping list will miss items

explanation.surface: A tired shopper who keeps forgetting things.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second definition as a play on the word read in two parts: without a list.
explanation.definitionFit: Listless means languid and lacking energy; read literally it describes a shopper with no list.

clue.text: Object to being given another posting?

definitions.meaning: second meaning, punning: sent again, as a letter re-posted

explanation.surface: Someone objecting to being transferred to a new job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Posting' sounds like a job transfer, but in the second sense it is mail that is RE-SENT.
explanation.definitionFit: To resent is to feel bitter about something; split as re-sent it means dispatched again.

clue.text: Tear down line in protest before I shut up

indicators.note: in places the single letter inside the following pair of pieces

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
L is the abbreviation for line
taken as written
sh is a call for silence

explanation.surface: Someone at a demonstration urges people to pull down a barrier, then falls silent.
explanation.walkthrough: The line goes between protest and I, and the call for quiet follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To demolish a building is to pull it down or tear it down.

clue.text: Workers securing financial support, first of all

indicators.note: securing means holding firmly, so the support is held inside

parts.note: men are workers
aid is support, often financial

explanation.surface: Employees getting money before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer works as an adjective, as in a maiden voyage or maiden speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A maiden voyage or speech is the very first one, so the word means first of all.

clue.text: Phrasing sign of spring in reference books

parts.note: diction is choice and phrasing of words
Aries is the zodiac sign beginning at the spring equinox

explanation.surface: Looking up words for spring in reference books.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictionaries are the standard reference books listing and defining words.

clue.text: String for one part of CD

wordplay.note: a single part of the abbreviation CD is either its first letter or its second, written out as words

explanation.surface: Asking for a length of cord to fit part of a CD.
explanation.walkthrough: One part of CD is either C or D: read that phrase as written and it spells the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cord is a length of thin rope or thick string.

clue.text: First person killed in confused situation after leader's removed

indicators.note: with the leader gone, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a babel is a scene of noisy confusion, after the Tower of Babel

explanation.surface: The first murder victim died in a chaotic scene once the chief was gone.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Abel was killed by his brother Cain, the first recorded homicide.

clue.text: Namely, short day in Rome

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: id est is Latin for namely, that is

explanation.surface: Specifying a short day in ancient Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin wordplay suits the Roman definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ides was a day in the Roman calendar, the 15th of some months and the 13th of others.

clue.text: Steps taken by fighters and a crew at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or adrift, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: all three words letter for letter

explanation.surface: Measures taken by combatants and a ship's crew out at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps' reads as measures, but it means dance steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A war dance is a ritual dance performed by warriors before battle, so its steps are taken by fighters.

clue.text: Listen in when broadcast is left-wing, in a way

indicators.note: broadcast suggests scattering seed, so the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: both words letter for letter

explanation.surface: Tuning in to a radio programme that turns out to be politically leftist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' tempts toward a sound-alike, but no pronunciation is involved.
explanation.definitionFit: Leninism is one form of communist ideology, so a Leninist is left-wing in a particular way.
